correctness.rationale: Every zero set is a nonattacking rook placement; the union of the neighborhoods of t chosen zeros contains exactly t(m+n-t-1) nonzero cells, giving the polynomial by inclusion-exclusion. The optimal coefficient is independently derived by exhaustive combinatorial classification of defender pairs and one-zero defenders; the total-condition boundary is proved by clique fibers. A separate direct-search verifier checked 558495 assignments and 44 symbolic parameter profiles.

originality.rationale: Full examination of the directly relevant preprint arXiv:2112.05476v1 (Theorem 3.4 and Section 3.3), and its open journal text (DOI:10.1007/s00009-022-02061-y), establishes the scalar optimum as previously known, but not the weighted count, minimum-function multiplicity, nor exact total/ordinary comparison. Searches for equivalent rook Roman weight enumeration and comparisons with complete multipartite enumerators did not locate a dominating statement. A future human priority check remains necessary.
residual_risks: Possible equivalent or stronger theorem under alternative Roman-domination terminology or rook-polynomial enumeration.

value.rationale: The weight enumerator is a natural full counting refinement of a known optimization invariant on a canonical Hamming/rook graph family. The parity-sensitive explicit count of all minimum functions reflects two distinct tight defending patterns, rather than a routine re-expression of a known scalar, and the polynomial yields every weight class and the total-variant boundary.
